messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: runtime-cluster — high pod eviction rate in 'runtime' namespace, multiple 'Evicted' events and container crashes reported. Auto-escalation to oncall.
marco: acked. I'm oncall for infra-sre, jumping in. any customer-facing errors yet?
katy: support here — seeing 5 customer error reports for generation timeouts (500s). Not sure if they correspond.
jess: i'm runtime-oncall, paging over. I see repeating CUDA OOM in some pods and also disk pressure events on nodes. grabbing logs.
marco: jess can you paste the kubectl outputs and a short log snippet?
jess: paste: ```
$ kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide
NAME                              READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
model-server-3-pt7k               0/1     Evicted   0          2h
model-server-7-k9lm               0/1     CrashLoopBackOff  12   1h
modelcache-0                      0/1     Evicted   0          1h30m
router-12                         1/1     Running   0          3d
```
And container log excerpt from model-server-7-k9lm: ```
2026-05-10T21:02:11Z ERROR runtime: failed to allocate KV cache
RuntimeError: cuCtxCreate failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
```
Also seeing write errors from modelcache: ```
ERROR IOError: [Errno 28] No space left on device: '/var/lib/model-cache/abc.idx'
```
ashley: node metrics show ephemeral usage at 97-99% on three nodes in the pool; i/o saturating due to lots of small writes from the modelcache writer + verbose debug logs during failures.
dan: possible attack vector: modelcache growth + unrotated logs. quick mitigation: reduce retention, rotate/remove old cache files, scale down cache replicas so we stop hitting multiple writers. we can also cordon+drain a node and delete large files.
marco: agree. jess, can you run a safe cleanup sequence and coordinate with infra? steps we want: 1) identify biggest dirs under /var/lib/model-cache and /var/log/containers, 2) trim modelcache to last N versions, 3) restart modelcache with env var to cap disk usage.
jess: running commands now — getting top consumers: ```
# on node runtime-n04
ssh root@runtime-n04 'sudo du -sh /var/lib/model-cache/* | sort -h | tail -n 20'
12G /var/lib/model-cache/ocr-large-v2
9.1G /var/lib/model-cache/translate-xl
6.3G /var/lib/model-cache/debug-dumps
```
I also ran `df -h`: ```
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/nvme0n1p1  200G  197G  1.5G  99% /
```
katy: customer impact — which endpoints are on those pods? we need an ETA and a short customer note.
marco: affected: text-generation API (models: ocr-large-v2 fallback to small-quant), embedding endpoint for translate-xl. mitigation: fallback routing to smaller variants configured, but will increase latency and lower quality. ETA for initial mitigation: ~20-30m.
support-bot: creating incident ticket on status page: INC-2026-117. Notifying customers tagged in error reports (via email template).
ashley: I'm going to cordon runtime-n04 and runtime-n05 to prevent scheduling while we clean. will drain any remaining non-critical pods.
jess: cleaned ~18G by removing old debug dumps and trimming translate-xl to one shard. restarting modelcache pod with `MODEL_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=4000000000` and `LOG_LEVEL=info` to avoid log sprawl.
dan: while that's running, a quick workaround to reduce CUDA OOMs: set per-pod `--max-sequence-len` lower or route traffic to smaller-quantized variant in the router, temporarily. I'll push a routing rule to send 30% to the small-quant model.
ml-runtime: applied canary routing change: `route:set text-gen:small-quant 30%` — observing queue drop now.
jess: after cleanup and restarts, node free space rose to ~12G and evictions stopped for the moment. still seeing occasional crashes from a server that lost its KV cache: `ERROR KeyError: cache miss for session` but it's degraded.
marco: status update for customers — katy, please send: short note explaining root cause (disk pressure -> pod evictions -> degraded runtime), mitigation (cleanup, routing fallback), ETA for full recovery and that we're investigating persistent logging and cache retention policies.
katy: sending now. email text: "We're investigating high error rates on text-generation; we've applied temporary routing fallbacks and freed disk on affected nodes. Expect service to be degraded but operational. We'll update in 30m."
support-bot: customers notified via status page update and support tickets updated.
ashley: monitoring: ephemeral usage trending down; i/o wait dropped from 80% to 12%. good sign.
marco: handing lead to jess for the incident. jess, you own the on-call for runtime followups. i'll stay on the thread for infra changes.
jess: taking lead. next actions: 1) scheduled node-level cleanup automation to remove cache versions older than 3, 2) add eviction threshold alarm at 85% ephemeral, 3) set kubelet evictionHard disk to 90% -> consider 92% via change request, 4) run an RCA doc.
dan: also propose we enable modelcache size limits per-pod (emptyDir size limit) and add logrotate enforced on /var/log/containers.
marco: noted. we should also audit why debug dumps were enabled by default for certain models — follow up with ml team.
ml-runtime: internal note: debug dumps were turned on for reproduce after last regression; will add guard so they don't run in prod.
jess: summary for now: evictions caused by ephemeral disk saturation from modelcache + debug logs -> removed 18G, restarted modelcache with a cap, applied routing fallback -> service degraded but recovering. will keep incident open for RCA items and postmortem.
katy: confirmed customers see improvement in error rates. closing customer-facing notification after final validation.
support-bot: incident INC-2026-117 updated: status = investigating -> mitigated (partial). follow-ups assigned.
marco: thanks team. last note: create a follow-up ticket with timeline and the commands we ran so SRE runbook can be updated.
jess: will file the postmortem and runbook changes. closing thread when RCA doc is up. :white_check_mark:
